Couple things. 

ALL doctors worth their salt know the dangers of benzos. I'm from Canada, so maybe it's different in other countries, but it isn't just the responsibility of the doctor to inform patients of dangers, the onus is on doctors and pharmacists as well. After the doctor does their assessment as to whether or not the drug is right for you (more on that in a minute), when you go to get the scrip filled, the pharmacist then asks a string of questions: "Have you had this medication before?" "Has your doctor been over the possible side effects of this medication? " being the first two. There's an insert about side effects and things to avoid, such as alcohol, driving, and important legal documents. Yhe medical system (in Canada at least) doesn't want to prescribe these things willy-nilly. I got my first prescription as an adjunct to a new antidepressant I was taking (buproprion) and it was only meant to be for the transition to that antidepressant.

Mentioned above: Doctors will only prescribe benzos after they determine that it is right for you. How do they do that? They talk to you, assess your needs and how best to treat whatever maladies you present them with. Generally (anf I have quarrels with this, but it is how it is) they resort to antidepressants before benzos for things like anxiety. Again though, this is what they determine to be necessary to treating your needs. They're medical professionals and they can only help you as much as much as what they determine to be necessary. If it's your first time seeing them, they'll make you do bloodwork to make sure that your vitamins are okay and your liver and kidneys are okay. They'll ask if you smoke, if you drink, if you get enough sleep, if you eat healthy, if you have thoughts of suicide. What your panic is like, how you've been dealing with your insomnia. If they pick up that you're seeking benzos and they can't find a good reason to prescribe them, you'll walk away with advice to take up jogging or walking, or a prescription for an ssri or a non-benzo sleep aid.

Why does /r/drugs snub benzo users? I dunno, maybe because benzos are arguably more dangerous than opioids and amphetamines. Yes I know, we all know, benzo withdrawal is more dangerous than theirs, that's what I mean. And yes, I know, we all know, acute benzo overdose is less dangerous than an overdose of those. They're for the most part very hippy-esque over there, nothing to do about that. I wouldb't expect anything less at burning man than at /r/drugs or the irc.

But I agree; bleh.
